answers.answer: Shuffle 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards into the initial draw deck. Put 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot. Start in 1st gear and draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 4–8: 'Shuffle your 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards together'; 'Place 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot'; 'Set Gear pawn to 1st gear'; 'Draw 7 cards'.

answers.answer: Shifting from 1st to 3rd is allowed and costs 1 Heat, associated with the Shift Gears step. The general Heat cycle indicates Engine-to-discard movement. Whether staying in the same gear is allowed is unsupported: the summary only describes moving up or down. Precise payment timing and an explicit source-zone rule for this shift payment are also unsupported.
answers.evidence: Step 1: 'Move your Gear pawn up or down one position. Shifting two positions costs 1 Heat.' Player Reference gives '1st to 3rd' as an example. Heat Card Cycle: 'Heat moves from Engine to discard to draw deck to hand'.

answers.answer: No. With enough playable cards, 3rd gear requires committing 3 cards, face down; choosing just two does not satisfy the requirement.
answers.evidence: Step 2: 'Play cards from hand face down equal to your gear number'; Player Reference: '3rd | 3'.

answers.answer: Shift Gears and Play Cards, steps 1–2, happen simultaneously. Steps 3–9 follow as a sequential phase, front car first. Whether each player completes all of steps 3–9 before the next starts is not explicitly established. Which side-by-side car acts first is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure headings: 'Simultaneous Phase (Steps 1-2)' and 'Sequential Phase (Steps 3-9, front car first)'. No side-by-side turn-order rule is supplied.

answers.answer: Cars cannot block passage. If the destination space is full, put your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. Prefer the spot closest to the Race Line when available.
answers.evidence: Blocked Movement: 'Cars never block passage' and 'first free spot behind the blocking cars'. Reveal & Move: 'Place car on the spot closest to the Race Line if available.'

answers.answer: Pass over the Heat and Starting Upgrade cards while flipping until the Speed 3 appears, so the Stress provides speed 3. The destinations of all three flipped cards are unsupported. The played Stress is a played card, so the generic Replenish Hand rule sends it from the Play Area to the discard pile at step 9. Its speed must be determined for Reveal & Move, step 3, before Adrenaline, step 4.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: 'flip cards from your draw deck until a Speed card appears; that card replaces the Stress card’s value'. Step 3 sums values before step 4 Adrenaline. Step 9: 'Move Play Area cards to discard pile'. No flipped-card destination rule is supplied.

answers.answer: The last two cars in a five-car race receive Adrenaline: each may add 1 extra speed and gains 1 extra Cooldown. The listed sequence places Adrenaline at step 4 before React/Boost at step 5. Whether its extra movement can instead be taken after boosting is unsupported. Whether unused Adrenaline can be saved for the next round is also unsupported.
answers.evidence: Step 4: 'Last car (or last 2 in 5+ player races) may add 1 extra speed and gain 1 extra Cooldown.' Step 5: 'Activate Cooldown and/or Boost symbols.'

answers.answer: In 2nd gear you have Cooldown 1 and can move the Heat card from your hand to your Engine during React. Boost costs 1 Heat. However, the ordering of Cooldown and Boost within React is unsupported, so the summary does not establish permission to cool that card and immediately spend it to Boost.
answers.evidence: Cooldown: 'Move Heat cards from your hand back to your Engine' and '2nd gear (Cooldown 1)'. React: 'Activate Cooldown and/or Boost symbols.' Boost: 'Pay 1 Heat'. No within-React ordering rule is supplied.

answers.answer: Boost is available once per turn and costs 1 Heat. Flip draw-deck cards until a Speed card appears and move according to that card; the added speed counts for corner checks. The Heat cycle points to the Engine as the source of spent Heat, but an explicit empty-Engine Boost rule is unsupported beyond the stated requirement to pay 1 Heat.
answers.evidence: Boost: 'Pay 1 Heat to flip cards from your draw deck until you reveal a Speed card; move your car accordingly. Once per turn. Increases speed for corner checks.' Heat Card Cycle: 'Heat moves from Engine to discard'.

answers.answer: Slipstream is optional. Check speed 6 because the two Slipstream spaces do not count toward corner speed. Against limit 4, pay 2 Heat.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'optionally move 2 spaces forward (does NOT count toward corner speed check)'. Check Corner: 'If you crossed a Corner Line, pay Heat equal to the difference between your speed and the corner’s Speed Limit (if exceeded)'.

answers.answer: The summary gives the excess-speed calculation but does not establish whether to check one or both of multiple crossed corners, nor their resolution order. Applying its calculation to both would yield 2 Heat for limit 6 plus 4 Heat for limit 4, totaling 6. Requiring that total is unsupported because the multiple-corner procedure is absent.
answers.evidence: Check Corner only says: 'If you crossed a Corner Line, pay Heat equal to the difference between your speed and the corner’s Speed Limit (if exceeded)'. It supplies no multiple-corner rule.

answers.answer: The corner requires 3 Heat, so having only 2 causes a Spin Out. Pay both remaining Heat cards; the general Heat cycle takes Heat from Engine to discard. Return the car to the first free space before the corner, take 2 Stress because you were in 4th gear, and set your gear to 1st. The zone receiving those new Stress cards is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 'pay all remaining Heat'; 'move car back to the first free space before the corner'; '2 Stress (3rd/4th gear)'; 'move Gear pawn to 1st gear'. Heat Card Cycle: 'Heat moves from Engine to discard'. No Stress destination is supplied.

answers.answer: You may voluntarily discard unwanted Speed cards during Discard, but may not discard Stress or Heat. Permission to browse your own or another player’s discard pile, and which information about those piles is public, are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Step 8: 'Optionally discard cards from hand (never Stress or Heat cards)'. No discard-pile inspection or public-information rule is supplied.

answers.answer: Move Play Area cards to the discard pile, then draw only enough cards to bring your hand back to 7.
answers.evidence: Step 9: 'Move Play Area cards to discard pile, draw back up to 7 cards.'

answers.answer: Immediately shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck, even before Replenish Hand. Do not include Play Area cards. The summary does not explicitly say to resume interrupted Stress flips after reshuffling, so that continuation is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Running Out of Cards: 'Shuffle discard pile into a new draw deck immediately (do not include Play Area cards)'. Stress Cards says to flip until a Speed card appears, but does not explicitly address continuing after a mid-resolution reshuffle.

answers.answer: Heat moves from Engine to discard, then through the draw deck into your hand. Cooldown returns Heat from hand to Engine. Normally you cannot play Heat or voluntarily discard it from your hand.
answers.evidence: Heat Card Cycle: 'Heat moves from Engine to discard to draw deck to hand; only returns to Engine via Cooldown'. Also: 'Heat cards can never be discarded or played from hand'. Cooldown moves Heat 'from your hand back to your Engine'.

answers.answer: Commit the two playable cards and cover the remaining two positions of the four-card commitment with Heat cards. Your car does not move. Set your gear to 1st and skip directly to step 9, where Play Area cards go to discard and you replenish your hand. Because you skip directly to step 9, you cannot use React to cool Heat this turn.
answers.evidence: Cluttered Hand: 'play what you can, cover the rest with Heat cards. Your car does not move; move Gear to 1st gear, skip to step 9'. Step 9: 'Move Play Area cards to discard pile, draw back up to 7 cards'.

answers.answer: Crossing first does not automatically win if multiple cars finish in the same round. The car furthest ahead wins; a side-by-side tie goes to the car closest to the Race Line. The summary says to place finished cars in order on the Hall of Fame, but exactly when they are removed from the track is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Victory Conditions: 'If multiple cars finish in the same round, the car furthest ahead wins (closest to Race Line breaks ties)'. Also: 'Continue playing until all cars finish; place finished cars in order on the Hall of Fame'. No precise removal timing is given.

answers.answer: The general Slipstream rule allows a qualifying two-space movement and the stated prohibition begins after crossing the final finish line, so the summary supports using Slipstream to cross that line. Once normal movement has crossed the final finish line, you cannot Slipstream afterward. Ignore speed limits beyond that final finish line.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'If you end next to or behind another car, optionally move 2 spaces forward'. Victory Conditions: 'After crossing the finish line on the final lap: no slipstreaming allowed; ignore speed limits after the finish line'.

answers.answer: Unsupported. The summary says the last two receive Adrenaline in a 5+ player race but does not establish whether that threshold uses the original number of cars/players or only cars still racing. It therefore does not resolve whether one or both remaining cars receives Adrenaline, or the determining car count.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: 'Last car (or last 2 in 5+ player races)'. No rule specifies how finished cars affect that count.
